ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the answer to this riddle? 'I am used to wash the body. I make bubbles and get smaller each time you use me.' (1 mark)
   A. a bucket
   B. a broom
   C. a towel
   D. soap

2. Which word has the long vowel /iː/? (1 mark)
   A. bit
   B. ship
   C. sheep
   D. sit

3. What does a dictionary give? (1 mark)
   A. A map of Kenya
   B. News about sports
   C. A list of names of people
   D. The meaning and spelling of words

4. Which is an opinion, not a fact? (1 mark)
   A. Boiled water is safer than untreated river water.
   B. Cold water is the nicest to drink.
   C. Soap helps to remove germs.
   D. Germs are too small to see.

5. Which word begins with the voiced sound /ð/? (1 mark)
   A. thumb
   B. this
   C. three
   D. think

6. Which is the best question for the answer 'In the school hall'? (1 mark)
   A. When did they practise?
   B. Whose hall is it?
   C. Who practised?
   D. Where did they practise?

7. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'very pretty'? (1 mark)
   A. beatiful
   B. beautiful
   C. butiful
   D. beutiful

8. Which word has a double r? (1 mark)
   A. necessary
   B. library
   C. tomorrow
   D. beautiful

9. Which word begins with the cluster 'br'? (1 mark)
   A. sweep
   B. clap
   C. grass
   D. broom

10. What does it mean to speak with expression? (1 mark)
   A. To speak without pausing
   B. To speak in a whisper only
   C. To use the voice to show meaning and feeling
   D. To speak very fast

11. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   B. A long story
   C. A kind of song
   D. A page of a dictionary

12. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the page
   B. The beat in the words
   C. The title
   D. The number of lines

13. In which person is a diary usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Second person (you)
   B. First person (I, we)
   C. No person
   D. Third person (he, she)

14. In the telephone game, why is careful listening important? (1 mark)
   A. The game is silent
   B. The message can change as it is passed on
   C. The first player wins by shouting
   D. There is nothing to hear

15. Which word has a silent k? (1 mark)
   A. king
   B. kind
   C. knee
   D. key

16. Which page of a magazine lists the articles and their page numbers? (1 mark)
   A. The contents page
   B. The advert page
   C. The cover
   D. The comic page

17. Which preposition completes: 'I am afraid ____ thieves.'? (1 mark)
   A. to
   B. at
   C. in
   D. of

18. Which preposition completes: 'He borrowed money ____ his uncle.'? (1 mark)
   A. from
   B. by
   C. of
   D. at

19. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who keeps money records? (1 mark)
   A. accountent
   B. accountant
   C. acounttant
   D. acountant

20. Which word ends with a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. class
   B. cla
   C. clasp
   D. clas

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Underline the prepositions: 'The children ran along the road, past the bank and into the market.' (3 marks)

22. Write two ways you can show a speaker that you are listening actively. (2 marks)

23. Write four sentences about your morning: two with have or has and two with had. (4 marks)

24. Write the steps you would follow to search for information safely online. (4 marks)

25. Name the five senses and say why a descriptive writer uses them. (3 marks)

26. Correct these sentences: (a) Who did scored the goal? (b) When you will come? (3 marks)

27. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

28. Explain why gestures should match your words. (2 marks)

29. Explain the difference between 'I have eaten' and 'I had eaten when he came.' (3 marks)

30. Give a situation in which 'Prevention is better than cure' applies. (2 marks)

31. Give a memory trick for spelling 'necessary' or 'separate'. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — soap
   Soap makes bubbles and wears away.

2. C — sheep
   'Sheep' has a long /iː/; the others have a short /ɪ/.

3. D — The meaning and spelling of words
   Dictionary words are in alphabetical order.

4. B — Cold water is the nicest to drink.
   An opinion says what someone thinks.

5. B — this
   'This' has the voiced 'th'.

6. D — Where did they practise?
   The answer names a place.

7. B — beautiful
   Beautiful is spelt b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l.

8. C — tomorrow
   'Tomorrow' is t-o-m-o-r-r-o-w.

9. D — broom
   'Broom' begins with b and r.

10. C — To use the voice to show meaning and feeling
   Expression means changing loudness, stress and pitch to show feeling.

11. A — A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   Proverbs teach lessons.

12. B — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

13. B — First person (I, we)
   A diary is about what I did and felt.

14. B — The message can change as it is passed on
   The last player may hear a different message.

15. C — knee
   In 'knee' the k is not pronounced.

16. A — The contents page
   The contents page shows where to find each article.

17. D — of
   We say 'afraid of'.

18. A — from
   We borrow from someone.

19. B — accountant
   Accountant has a double c.

20. A — class
   Class ends in ss.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: along, past, into
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and nod; keep still and quiet; say 'I see'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have brushed my teeth. She has swept the floor. We had eaten before we left. He had washed before school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what to find out; choose key words; use an approved site; read carefully and note the facts in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sight, sound, smell, touch and taste. They help the reader to imagine the thing being described.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the senses and 1 for the reason.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) Who scored the goal? (b) When will you come?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correction and 1 for question marks and capitals.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is reading quickly to get the main idea; scanning is looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: If they do not match, the listener may be confused about what you mean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for confusion and 1 for a clear reason.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'I have eaten' says the eating is finished and it matters now. 'I had eaten when he came' says I finished eating before he came, in the past.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for the time link.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands before eating prevents illness, which is better than getting sick and needing medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a situation and 1 for linking it to the proverb.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: 'Necessary' has one collar (c) and two sleeves (ss); 'separate' has 'a rat' in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trick and 1 for a correct explanation.
